title: Conflicting requirements for urllib3
body:
In origin/main ee93fac6b2f7 I find conflicting required urllib3 version information:

```
setup.cfg:10:    urllib3>=1.21.1,<1.27
setup.py:64:    "urllib3>=1.21.1,<3",
```

Shouldn't both files have the same restrictions?

Best regards

Heinrich

title: API-provided proxies are silently overridden by environment variables; no per-request opt-out
body:
Summary
Requests automatically uses environment proxies from HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, etc. There is currently no clean per-request way to disable this behavior. The only reliable workaround is to create a Session and set ```session.trust_env = False.```

Current behavior
When proxy-related environment variables are present, a simple request such as:
```
requests.get(url, proxies={})
```
still uses the environment proxy. Passing an empty proxies dict does not mean “disable all proxies”; it means “no API-level proxy was provided”, so environment proxies are merged in by Session.merge_environment_settings() when trust_env is True.

To actually bypass environment proxies, users must write:

```
session = requests.Session()
session.trust_env = False
session.get(url)
```
They cannot write:

```

title: Encoding of escaped values in parameter?
body:
Hi,

I get a token from a server that's something like "FOO%3D". I need to return this token to the server as is, but when I set this value as a parameter to a URL, requests encodes the `%` as `%25`, so the string that gets sent is "FOO%253D". I see that there was an issue regarding this kind of thing (https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/5461) and it seems to have been resolved as to always encode the percent as if it were a literal, rather than part of the escaped value (%3D in my case).

Is there some decent way I can send the token as a parameter literally without requests trying to re-interpret what I've provided?

Thanks,
